\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{উঁকি} \bn{দেওয়া} (ũki deoyā)}{উঁকি দেওয়া (ũki deoyā)}]{\bn{উঁকি} \bn{দেওয়া} (ũki deoyā) — to peep; to peek}

\label{lesson:BN-C286-uki-deoya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to loot, then the Bengali for fraud.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{উঁকি} \bn{দেওয়া}}
\textbf{\bn{উঁকি} \bn{দেওয়া}} — \emph{ũki deoyā} — \textquotedblleft{}to peep; to peek\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আওয়াজ} \bn{শুনে} \bn{আমি} \bn{জানালা} \bn{দিয়ে} \bn{উঁকি} \bn{দিলাম।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āoyāj shune āmi jānālā diye ũki dilām.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I heard a noise and peeped out of the window.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{শিশু} \bn{জানালা} \bn{দিয়ে} \bn{উঁকি} \bn{দিল}, \emph{sei shishu jānālā diye ũki dilô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{উঁকি} \bn{দেওয়া}} (\emph{ũki deoyā}) puts \bn{উঁকি} — filed in CDIAL 1938 under Sanskrit \emph{udīkṣā}, 'looking up', where a Bengali \emph{uki}, 'careful watching', appears — before \bn{দেওয়া}: to give a peep.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ũki deoyā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ũki deoyā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āoyāj shune āmi jānālā diye ũki dilām.} — I heard a noise and peeped out of the window.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to loot, then the Bengali for fraud, then say \emph{ũki deoyā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{উঁকি} \bn{দেওয়া} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To peep; to peek\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{প্রদর্শন} \bn{করা} (prôdôrshôn kôrā)}{প্রদর্শন করা (prôdôrshôn kôrā)}]{\bn{প্রদর্শন} \bn{করা} (prôdôrshôn kôrā) — to display; to exhibit}

\label{lesson:BN-C286-prodorshon-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for fraud, then the Bengali for to peep.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{প্রদর্শন} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{প্রদর্শন} \bn{করা}} — \emph{prôdôrshôn kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to display; to exhibit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{শিল্পী} \bn{তাঁর} \bn{নতুন} \bn{ছবিগুলো} \bn{প্রদর্শন} \bn{করলেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shilpī tā̃r nôtun chhôbigulo prôdôrshôn kôrlen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The artist put his new paintings on show.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{ছবিগুলো} \bn{প্রদর্শন} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini chhôbigulo prôdôrshôn kôrlen}.

\bn{প্রদর্শনী}, an exhibition, is built on the same noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{প্রদর্শন} \bn{করা}} (\emph{prôdôrshôn kôrā}) puts \bn{প্রদর্শন} — Sanskrit \emph{pradarśana}, \emph{pra} 'forth' with \emph{darśana} 'a seeing', so a showing (Monier-Williams), taken over whole — before \bn{করা}, to do: to put something on show.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prôdôrshôn kôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prôdôrshôn kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shilpī tā̃r nôtun chhôbigulo prôdôrshôn kôrlen.} — The artist put his new paintings on show.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for fraud, then the Bengali for to peep, then say \emph{prôdôrshôn kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{প্রদর্শন} \bn{করা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To display; to exhibit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{অদ্ভুত} (ôdbhut)}{অদ্ভুত (ôdbhut)}]{\bn{অদ্ভুত} (ôdbhut) — strange; odd}

\label{lesson:BN-C286-odbhut}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to peep, then the Bengali for to exhibit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{অদ্ভুত}}
\textbf{\bn{অদ্ভুত}} — \emph{ôdbhut} — \textquotedblleft{}strange; odd\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{সেই} \bn{রাতে} \bn{আমরা} \bn{পুকুরের} \bn{পাশে} \bn{একটা} \bn{অদ্ভুত} \bn{আলো} \bn{দেখলাম।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sei rāte āmrā pukurer pāshe ekṭā ôdbhut ālo dekhlām.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
That night we saw a strange light beside the pond.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{অদ্ভুত}} (\emph{ôdbhut}) is Sanskrit \emph{adbhuta}, 'extraordinary, wonderful' (Monier-Williams); in Bengali it leans towards odd and uncanny.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôdbhut}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôdbhut}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sei rāte āmrā pukurer pāshe ekṭā ôdbhut ālo dekhlām.} — That night we saw a strange light beside the pond.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to peep, then the Bengali for to exhibit, then say \emph{ôdbhut} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{অদ্ভুত} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Strange; odd\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ছায়া} (chhāyā)}{ছায়া (chhāyā)}]{\bn{ছায়া} (chhāyā) — a shadow; shade}

\label{lesson:BN-C286-chhaya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to exhibit, then the Bengali for strange.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ছায়া}}
\textbf{\bn{ছায়া}} — \emph{chhāyā} — \textquotedblleft{}a shadow; shade\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{রাতে} \bn{বারান্দায়} \bn{একটা} \bn{লম্বা} \bn{ছায়া} \bn{দেখে} \bn{আমি} \bn{ভয়} \bn{পেলাম।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rāte bārāndāy ekṭā lômbā chhāyā dekhe āmi bhôy pelām.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I got scared when I saw a long shadow on the veranda at night.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ছায়া}} (\emph{chhāyā}) is Sanskrit \emph{chāyā}, 'shade, shadow' (Monier-Williams), unchanged. It is also the cool shade of a tree: \bn{গাছের} \bn{ছায়ায়}, in the shade of a tree.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chhāyā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chhāyā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rāte bārāndāy ekṭā lômbā chhāyā dekhe āmi bhôy pelām.} — I got scared when I saw a long shadow on the veranda at night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to exhibit, then the Bengali for strange, then say \emph{chhāyā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{লক্ষ} \bn{করা} (lôkkhô kôrā)}{লক্ষ করা (lôkkhô kôrā)}]{\bn{লক্ষ} \bn{করা} (lôkkhô kôrā) — to observe; to watch closely}

\label{lesson:BN-C286-lokkho-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for strange, then the Bengali for a shadow.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{লক্ষ} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{লক্ষ} \bn{করা}} — \emph{lôkkhô kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to observe; to watch closely\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{পুলিশ} \bn{অনেক} \bn{দিন} \bn{ধরে} \bn{বাড়িটা} \bn{লক্ষ} \bn{করছিল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pulish ônek din dhôre bāṛiṭā lôkkhô kôrchhilô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police had been watching the house for many days.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{লোকটাকে} \bn{লক্ষ} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini lokṭāke lôkkhô kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{লক্ষ} \bn{করা}} (\emph{lôkkhô kôrā}) puts Sanskrit \emph{lakṣa}, 'a mark, a target' (Monier-Williams), before \bn{করা}: to make something your mark, to keep your eyes on it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lôkkhô kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pulish ônek din dhôre bāṛiṭā lôkkhô kôrchhilô.} — The police had been watching the house for many days.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for strange, then the Bengali for a shadow, then say \emph{lôkkhô kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{লক্ষ} \bn{করা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To observe; to watch closely\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
